content.title: Ohio State vs TCU highlights: Horned Frogs defeat Buckeyes in March Madness
content.text: Updated March 19, 2026, 4:14 p.m. ETBe sure to follow USA TODAY Sports' live blog keeping track of all of NCAA Tournament's Day 1 games.First-round action from the 2026 NCAA Tournament kicked off with a bang.Xavier Edmonds sank the game-winning field goal for No. 9 TCU to give it a 66-64 win over No. 8 Ohio State, on Thursday, March 19, from Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, South Carolina. Buckeyes' guard Bruce Thornton missed the game-tying 3-pointer.The Horned Frogs will move on to the second round on Saturday, playing the winner of No. 1 Duke and No. 16 Siena.Watch select NCAA Tournament games on Fubo (free trial)TCU led by as many as 15 points in the first half, but saw Ohio State storm back in the second half to take a 5-point lead at 55-50 with 6:19 left. However, the Horned Frogs were able to hang on for the victory on Edmonds' game-winner.Micah Robinson — who gave TCU a brief lead at 64-61 before a Thornton 3-pointer — finished with 18 points and five rebounds, while Collins and David Punch each added 16 points. Punch and Collins had 13 and 8 rebounds, respectively.John Mobley Jr. led the Buckeyes with 15 points and six assists, while Devin Royal added 14 points and Amare Bynum finished with 12. Bruce Thornton, who was averaging 20.2 points per game, was limited to just 10 points on 3-of-9 shooting.USA TODAY brought you updates from the 2026 NCAA Tournament first-round matchup between the Horned Frogs and Buckeyes. Catch up here. Xavier Edmonds gives TCU leadXavier Edmonds knocks down a layup with 4.1 seconds left to give TCU a 66-64 lead. OSU calls a timeout for one last shot. TCU-OSU tied with 26 seconds leftMicah Robinson and Bruce Thornton exchange 3-pointers and the game is tied 64-all with 26 seconds left in the game. Thorton's 3-pointer comes after Robinson gives TCU the lead.The Horned Frogs have the ball and a chance at the final shot following this timeout. David Punch, TCU re-take leadDavid Punch's layup helps TCU re-take a 58-57 lead over Ohio State with 3:45 left in the game. The Buckeyes call a timeout, which leads to a media timeout.This should be a good ending between the Horned Frogs and the Buckeyes. Ohio State takes lead over TCUOhio State has its first lead since it was 5-2 in the opening minute of the first half following a basket from Amare Bynum. The Buckeyes lead the Horned Frogs 51-50 with 7:05 left in the game.Bynum is up to 12 points with nine rebounds to lead the Buckeyes. Xavier Edmonds, who has 11 points, picks up his fourth foul and will be on the bench for a little while for TCU. TCU calls timeout as OSU cuts lead to 2We have a game now. The Buckeyes have cut the lead to two points with 8:40 left in the game. TCU calls a timeout following a 3-pointer from Gabe Cupps to cut the lead to 49-47.Ohio State is on a 7-0 run and outscoring the Horned Frogs 23-10 in the second half. Ohio State fights back into gameOhio State used a 10-0 scoring run to cut the TCU lead to 43-40 with 12:42 left in the game. However, TCU's Jayden Pierre hits a 3-pointer before the media timeout to extend the lead back to six.The Buckeyes have outscored the Horned Frogs 16-7 in the second half. Ohio State cuts lead to 10 at second media timeoutOhio State cuts the lead to 43-33 with 14:10 left in the game. The Buckeyes have outscored the Horned Frogs 9-4 in the second half to stay within reach.John Mobley Jr. hit his second 3-pointer of the game on the last OSU possession. TCU is shooting 1-for-10 in the second half. TCU leads by 13 in second halfBoth teams have combined for just six points in over four minutes into the second half at the first media timeout. The Horned Frogs lead 41-28 with 15:56 left in the game.TCU is shooting 1-for-8 in the half, while the Buckeyes are shooting 2-of-6. OSU is shooting just 35.3% for the game from the field and 15.4% from 3-point range. Second half underway between OSU-TCUOhio State scores four straight points to open the second half to cut the TCU lead to 39-28. Still a long ways to go for the Buckeyes.
